programmes.d: Team Salvage embark on a titanic 4-day rescue mission to resurrect a 20-ton, 40 ft yacht that sank 12 years ago half a kilometer offshore. In the most epic challenge of their career, the crew face up to the ultimate salvage mission impossible.
Allen and Ton trek to an auction in Moreno Valley, CA, where two locker wins yield a vintage jukebox, a valuable baseball card, and a Prohibition-era moonshine still.
Barely making it to an auction in Corona, CA, Allen and Ton buy an overstuffed unit and find an antique crossbow, a rare 10-gauge Winchester shotgun, and a 1940s Kiss-o-Meter.
Extreme Quadzilla ATV, the fastest 4 wheeler ever; a 1910s Remington Derringer and a 1880s Palm Squeezer pistol; revolutionary 1800s Western Electric telephone with a crank dial.
1905 Hand-crank Thomas Edison gramophone with cylindrical records; a discontinued Addictor 190 Mini Boat; a rare 1897 Regina music box.
Tempers flare and prices soar as the buyers confront aggressive guest auctioneer Jeff Schwartz, aka “The Liquidator.”
Guest auctioneer Patrick Pecker brings “the full Pecker” to the auction, fuelling his longstanding feud with Roy.
Roy suits up in full army gear to declare war on the buyers in Scarborough.
Roy’s paltry gifts are no match for Cindy’s foul mood at the auction in Scarborough.
The Thornhill buyers run for cover when a self-help CD gives Roy a new lease on his egomaniacal life.
A Brampton auction near some of the gang’s old high school proves they’re all still rowdy teenagers at heart.
Paul’s locker addiction reaches new highs (and lows) at the Wasaga Beach auction.
Rick and Cindy bring a psychic to help them land the best lockers in Don Mills.
In this special episode, Team Salvage countdown the top 10 toughest, dirtiest and most hardcore salvage missions in their history.

Team Salvage has been called in to rescue a stranded vessel stuck in a mangrove jungle in North Queensland. It got blown in there by Cyclone Debbie. The only way they can get it out is to winch it out. But there’s a problem.
Further investigation suggests a link between the mysterious medieval cross and the Knights Templar.
A skeleton key and maps from Fred Nolan's archives open a new door in the Lagina's quest, while new evidence suggests a Templar connection to the lead cross found in Smith's Cove.
The plot thickens around the discovery of the lead cross as a new theory points to possible ancient origins. Rick pulls an artifact from the swamp that may support one of Fred Nolan's theories.

The discovery of the mysterious lead cross raised new questions about a Knights Templar connection. Tonight, we take a look at Templar history and the compelling Templar clues the team has found so far.
It's all hands on deck in the Money Pit as the team hits something in the DMT shaft that may prove to be the last thing standing between it and the answers below.
Harley Davidson V-twin EVO engine and revolutionary 1958 dual-suspension swingarm frame; '80s Ms. Pac-Man arcade machine; rare Air Jordan vintage shoe collection in mint condition.
1978 Williams Disco pinball machine; 1898 dice popper gambling device; talking 1990s bar top breathalyzer; deadly fishing harpoon.
All-terrain Air Commander Hovercraft, a 1970s NASA countdown clock and a one-of-a-kind 1960s Delta Relay rocket.
Metal Victorian-era burial casket; 1870s glass fire extinguisher grenades; a mechanical 1896 handcrafted Chicago fire station alarm box.
Scale RC Viper FanJet aircraft with a potent jet engine; 1920s Gundlach Korona large format field camera used for photography expeditions. Ton pilots a plane, but crashes and burns.
The 1930s "blasting machine" dynamite detonator box; 1890s treasure chest with secret compartments. Ton smelts jewelry to forge bricks of silver.
The first pump-action shotgun - a Winchester Model 1897; a hunter's collection of prize big game, full-body taxidermy.
